newsitem.title: USA: USWC gasolines ease as NYMEX sidelines buyers.
newsitem.headline: USWC gasolines ease as NYMEX sidelines buyers.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot unleaded gasoline prices eased in quiet Wednesday discussion after a volatile futures market forced traders to the sidelines, brokers said.
NYMEX March heating oil futures shed 1.01 cents a gallon from sharp morning gains, trading around 60.90 cents at 1200 PST Wednesday.
The volatile contract scared off West Coast players, who left the market with few deals heard done.
"It's very quiet because of the Merc," one broker said, adding he heard Feb CARB diesel done around 80/81 cents.
Gasolines meanwhile weakend in Los Angeles, with sellers of March conventional unleaded dropping their asking price one cent a gallon to 74 cents.
San Francisco conventional stood at parity with L.A, traders said.
And bids for March CARB grade gasoline in L.A. eased a half cent to 74 cents a gallon, with February barrels seen two cents lower.
March barrels of gasoline carried the two-cent premium because changes in vapor pressure requirements are expected to result in lower production of second cycle March gasoline.
